column5: ★ THE GSE MF BOOK SPLIT IN TWO IN Q2-2026, AND THE SPLIT IS THE EVIDENCE. Fannie MF serious DQ FELL to 0.60% (from 0.78% Q1) while Freddie MF DQ ROSE to 0.51% (from 0.44% Q4-25) — same quarter, same asset class, opposite directions. Fannie's own release attributes its decline "primarily as a result of the modification of a loan portfolio previously in forbearance and foreclosure activity, partially offset by additional loans that became seriously delinquent due to sustained market challenges" — BOTH named channels remove loans from the numerator with ZERO borrower cures, and the newly-serious inflow continued. Decisive corroboration: Fannie's MF credit-loss provision ROSE 49% QoQ ($174M->$259M) on "weaker property valuations and slower NOI growth" IN THE SAME QUARTER the DQ rate fell. A healing book does not reserve 49% harder against itself.

column5: ★ A STALE-YEAR ARTICLE CAN FALSELY CONFIRM YOUR OWN PREDICTION — the dangerous direction of the year-trap. Searching for the FMHPI June-2026 print (HOM-01 Leg-1's first resolver, due that day), the index returned CalculatedRisk's "Freddie Mac House Price Index Declined in June; Up 2.0% Year-over-year" THREE times across three differently-worded queries, with the engine's summary layer restating it in the present tense as the 2026 print. Direct fetch: publication date 2025-07-31, June-2025 data. Those figures (June 2.0% vs May 2.3%) would have graded J<M = "Leg-1 CONFIRMED." The real June-2026 print had not posted.
column6: Direct WebFetch of the CalculatedRisk article showing pub date 2025-07-31, vs three search-summary assertions of 2026
column11: WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE SPAWN-5 ERROR: that misread felt surprising enough to stress-test; a figure that CONFIRMS your prior does not trigger the re-check instinct. TWO HIGH-RISK TRIGGERS: (a) annually-recurring releases whose PRIOR-YEAR article has a near-identical headline shape (monthly HPI, quarterly DQ surveys) — search relevance cannot separate them; (b) a resolver you are actively waiting on, where "the print is out" is the outcome you WANT. A prediction's resolver is the single worst place to accept a search summary. Correct outcome here was already written in the grading sheet's own "release delayed/missing" row: do not grade, do not substitute Case-Shiller or FHFA, report NOT-GRADEABLE as a real result.

column11: DEFINITIONS DIVERGE TOO, so the collision is not merely cosmetic: SF = 90+ days OR in foreclosure, by LOAN COUNT (footnote 10); MF = 60+ days, by UNPAID PRINCIPAL BALANCE (footnote 11). The UPB basis is why ONE modified portfolio swung the MF rate 18bps — a count-based metric would not have moved like that. RULE: never cite a GSE delinquency figure without stating BOOK (SF/MF) and BASIS (count/UPB) in the same breath. This trap nearly bit during this very session's Fannie pull, where a search summary returned "0.60% as of June 30 2026" without saying which book.
